purpose: Assess a primary Caraga freshwater-market inventory for useful, source-bounded fish supply and waterbody-origin context while preventing market sale from being mistaken for direct occurrence or a site-specific fish survey.

source.title: Freshwater Fishes in Traditional Markets of the Largest Urban City of Caraga Region, Philippines

methodsAndScope.samplingSchedule: Opportunistic weekend market visits, Saturdays and Sundays, 07:00-18:00 local time.
methodsAndScope.sites: Twelve Butuan City markets: three major public markets and nine local artisanal markets (talipapa). Figure 1 is a market map, not a catch-site map.
methodsAndScope.speciesSummary: The article reports 15 freshwater-fish names across 12 families. At least 10 representative fish per species per market were selected for morphometric measurement; the paper says an expert verified identifications. The displayed account does not provide museum voucher accession numbers or a specimen-to-catch-waterbody chain.
methodsAndScope.tableCoverage: Table 1 lists 15 fish names. Table 2 displays 12 data rows representing 11 distinct names because Glossogobius giuris is split into juvenile and adult rows. Encrasicholina oligobranchus, Muraenesox cinereus, Pangasianodon hypophthalmus and Johnius borneensis do not receive their own Table 2 market-metric rows, although three appear in the broad prose provenance grouping.
methodsAndScope.marketInterviews: Vendor interviews recorded local fish names, source location, captured/cultured origin, gear, supply, demand and price. Consent and BFAR-Caraga research authorization are described.
methodsAndScope.evidenceType: Market observation, procured market samples, vendor-reported supply provenance and market metrics; this is not direct sampling of all named source waters and not a current waterbody-wide checklist.

reportedSpecificOrigins.sourceClaim: Results prose says the fish was harvested in Lake Mainit; Table 2 uses source code i for Lake Mainit.
reportedSpecificOrigins.evidenceType: Vendor-reported market supply origin as represented by the article.
reportedSpecificOrigins.limitation: Not an independently documented Lake Mainit capture event, station or dated field observation.

reportedSpecificOrigins.sourceClaim: Results prose says it came from Agusan Marsh. Table 2 lists source codes h and i; the caption glossary defines these as Kitcharao and Lake Mainit.
reportedSpecificOrigins.evidenceType: Conflicting vendor-reported provenance within the article.
reportedSpecificOrigins.limitation: Do not choose one source or assign this fish to Agusan Marsh, Kitcharao or Lake Mainit until the discrepancy is resolved.

reportedSpecificOrigins.sourceClaim: Results prose groups these as captured from an estuary of Lumbocan and the Agusan River. Table 2 supplies locality-source codes such as Lumbocan and Masao, but no catch station, exact river reach or specimen-level source assignment.
reportedSpecificOrigins.limitation: The article does not support assigning each listed taxon to one exact river, estuary, station or salinity condition. Preserve `Yarica hyalosoma` as printed pending a separate taxonomy review.

waterbodyProvenance.interpretation: Waterbody names in this paper describe reported market supply sources, not independently sampled ecological occurrences. The market location is not the fish capture location.

limitations: A market presence demonstrates sale/availability in a surveyed market during the study window, not wild presence, abundance, recruitment or current status in nearby rivers and lakes.
The study's weekend, daytime, opportunistic market schedule does not establish year-round survey coverage; vendor estimates about market availability are a distinct evidence type.
No voucher accession, museum repository, specimen-to-taxon image archive, genetic identification or specimen-to-catch-site chain is reported in the reviewed article.
The article conflicts on the reported source of Cyprinus carpio: Agusan Marsh in the prose versus Kitcharao and Lake Mainit in the Table 2 source-code key.
Table 2 contains 11 unique fish names, fewer than the 15 names in Table 1; four Table 1 names have no individual Table 2 market-metric row.
The Lumbocan/Agusan River estuary grouping is not a complete species-by-waterbody or station crosswalk.
Source-reported native/introduced categories, IUCN assessments, scarcity claims and legal interpretations were not independently verified and are not imported as Bangwit guidance.
The official article page returned HTTP 403 to the review fetcher; the official full-text PDF and indexed publisher metadata were accessible. No access control was bypassed.

The article does not display a Creative Commons license. The journal's Author's Guide says authors sign a copyright-transfer form upon acceptance; no item-specific reuse permission for app/database extraction was verified.

decision.sourceType: Primary market inventory and vendor-interview study.

nextAction: Retain this as a market-supply and provenance-context source only. Resolve the Cyprinus carpio source conflict and review the 15 article labels against fish taxonomy authorities as a separate step; do not convert vendor origins into direct waterbody occurrence rows.

references.supports: Official PJS article metadata, authors, DOI and abstract. The page itself returned HTTP 403 during this review; search-indexed publisher metadata was used only for bibliographic cross-checking.
Primary full text for the 2023 market methods, market counts, species inventory, vendor-origin coding, named source claims and internal Cyprinus carpio provenance conflict.
